caption:
Real marble or printed porcelain: the edge gives the price away.

Stone is the same all the way through, so a vein carries over every edge and down the side. A printed porcelain face stops at the cut, and the edge shows a plain body. Ask to see a sample edge before you pay for a slab.

Through-body porcelain is the exception, and on a kitchen floor it is often the better buy. It does not etch when lemon meets it.

Save this for the stone yard.
